a#U.text:
INSTRUCTIONS

Press E to toggle the Editor Mode. (Press it again to switch it off.)

• VARIABLES

At the top left, the 4 variables represent, from top to bottom:
The player's X Speed, Y Speed, X Position and Y Position.

At the bottom left, you can change the speed at which the game runs.

The top right shows the current time (3x more precise than the original timer)

• EDIT INPUTS

The strings represent, in that order, Left, Up, Right, Down, # Frames.
For the 4 first strings, a 1 means that the key is held; a 0 means it isn't.
The last string tells how many frames the keys are kept that way.

• SAVESTATES

Press keys 1 / 2 / 3 to save the current state of the game.
Press keys 6 / 7 / 8 to go back to (load) their respective savestate.

This is useful because it avoids starting over every time we test something.

Warning! Do not load a state which was saved before the most recent green flag click. That would make moving platforms and enemies disappear.

• BUGS

If you load a savestate during the death animation, the TAS will desync. To fix that, simply load the state again.

If you load a savestate from far away, the objects (floor, spikes, etc.) may not appear instantly. This is only a visual bug, so it's fine.

You might get killed for seemingly no reason when loading a savestate. This is due to the spikes' 1-frame delay before their repositioning. If it happens, wait for the end of the death animation (↑) and load the state again.

Dynamic objects respond very badly to savestate loading and saving, and I don't know why. When testing inputs where the position of a dynamic object matters, I suggest starting the TAS over and notice on which exact frame the object is at a significant spot in the cycle. Then, when loading a savestate, look if the frame count desynced. Press M to make the object move one iteration if it's lagging behind.

a!R.text: Put this at the top of your script to make objects move (legitimately) without having to wait super long for a cycle before starting. You need at least one frame of standing still beforehand though.
